title: Forrest Valora: OU's All-Big Eight Tight End and Orange Bowl Hero
question: Who was Forrest Valora at Oklahoma?
answer: Forrest Valora was an Oklahoma tight end from Phoenix, Arizona, on the roster from 1977 to 1980. He was first-team All-Big Eight as a senior in 1980 and caught the two-point pass that won the 1981 Orange Bowl.
summary: Phoenix native Forrest Valora was OU's tight end in Barry Switzer's wishbone, a 1980 first-team All-Big Eight pick, and the man who caught the 1981 Orange Bowl winner.
body: Forrest Valora came to Norman from Phoenix, Arizona, and was on Oklahoma's roster from 1977 through the 1980 season. He played tight end for Barry Switzer from 1978 on, wearing No. 82.
As a 6-0, 233-pound senior in 1980, Valora was named the first-team tight end on United Press International's All-Big Eight team.

His most famous catch came in his final college game. In the January 1, 1981 Orange Bowl, Oklahoma trailed No. 2 Florida State 17-16 after a late touchdown, and Switzer went for two. J.C. Watts threw to Valora in the end zone, and the Sooners held on to win 18-17.

That spring the Green Bay Packers picked Valora in the 11th round of the 1981 NFL Draft, the 282nd selection. PackerStats lists him as signed on June 1 and released on Aug. 29, 1981, before the season began.
For Sooners fans who remember that night in Miami, though, Valora's place in OU history was already secure.
